configuration: Separate Fed/daily Treasury pilot; 36/12 train/validation statements, 180/60 windows, matched seeds 23–25 and 10 fixed epochs. Four paired cells, shared frozen yield branch, gate fit on chronological train-only OOF predictions.

figure.alt: Validation MAE: no change 9.950 bp, frozen yields 11.830, pooled 11.787 ungated and 11.810 gated, cross-attention 12.200 ungated and 11.976 gated.

finding: No change led at 9.950 bp MAE. Cross-attention was 0.413 bp worse than pooled without a gate, and 0.166 bp worse with one. The gate softened the cross-attention penalty but did not rescue it. Prior-statement text matched or slightly beat the current statement in all four cells.
limitations: Repeated validation only: 12 statements and overlapping origins; no held-out test, no C1/equity result, no verified historical minute-level availability. Paired bootstrap is descriptive.
question: Does querying individual statement tokens from frozen yield history improve over pooled text, with and without a learned gate?
title: Compact Treasury: cross-attention and gate ablation
